newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico debt issuers seen testing market waters.
newsitem.headline: Mexico debt issuers seen testing market waters.

text.p: A wide range of Mexican corporate and sovereign borrowers are seen testing the waters in credit markets in the short-term, with the first up likely being the federal government, analysts said on Monday.
The United Mexican States (UMS), the official name of the federal government, is seen placing a 500 billion lira 20-year bond issues this week, they said.
That issue will be led by Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
A long list of corporates are also seen ready to float various types of debt issues.

Mexican steel company Altos Hornos de Mexico (Ahmsa) has already negotiated a $330 million export-backed credit and the deal will be sealed within days, a company official said on Monday. That two-tranche deal was arranged by J.P. Morgan.
The heavily indebted company also has been putting together a two-tranche Yankee bond, probably worth $200 million, sources said.
One of the tranches could be between five and seven years and the other for seven to ten years.
That Yankee bond is seen led by Merrill Lynch and Santander, and will be used to replace a bridge loan negotiated by Santander, analysts said.
A company official said the deal may be put off until the interest rate outlook in the United States calms, unless a window of opportunity opens.

Paper products producer Copamex Industries S.A. also is seen issuing a $200 million, seven-year Eurobond, an issue that has already received a BB credit rating from Standard & Poor's and a B1 rating from Moody's.
"This will be the first time both Ahmsa and Copamex will issue straight debt issues," said Anne Milne, ING Barings head of Latin America corporate debt research.
"It will help increase the number of names in the market," she said.
Another Mexican company, Fideicomiso Petacalco, a trust set up to build and run a coal receiving and handling terminal in Mexico, is also seen launching $316 million in senior secured notes.
The terminal will be used to supply coal to the Petacalco Power Station, which is operated by the government agency, Comision Federal de Electricidad (CFE).
The note has received a Ba2 long-term debt rating from Moody's.
Moody's said Petacalco's high credit rating is based on the CFE's rating, which is equal to the current sovereign ceiling.
